quote: the requirements to qualify are to have a form of taxable income and a credit score of six fifty or higher. Would that be the case for you and your wife?
stewart_read: Rep states 650 as the qualifying credit threshold, matching the exact same drift already logged in SESSION18_fcbf33c1 (Meg), where the schema's documented threshold is 670. This is now a second confirmed instance of the same misstatement, which strengthens the case that this is a live floor-wide drift rather than one rep's error.
alternative_hypothesis: This could be a one-off misspeak by this individual rep rather than a systemic issue.
coaching_implication: Flag to Kenny as a recurring schema_drift_detection pattern (now 2 documented calls) — confirm whether 650 or 670 is the current active policy, since reps are inconsistently stating both.

quote: Is there anyone else on the title of the home with you at all?
stewart_read: The verify question is asked correctly but the customer's answer ('It's been a while') doesn't resolve it — no co-owner is confirmed or denied. The rep then unilaterally assumes a spouse exists two minutes later ('you and your wife') without ever having established that fact on the call.
alternative_hypothesis: The ASR may have mangled a clearer answer the customer actually gave (e.g., 'my wife's been on it a while'), in which case the rep's later reference to 'your wife' would be grounded rather than assumed.
coaching_implication: Regardless of ASR quality, the rep should have explicitly re-confirmed co-ownership before assuming a spouse and before any appointment/callback is set — if a spouse is on title, protocols.spouse_decision requires she be included in the eventual appointment, and right now nothing establishes whether she exists, will be reachable, or will be on the callback.

quote: I would say about 3¢ a month.
stewart_read: The transcript renders the bill figure as '3¢,' almost certainly an ASR error given the rep's immediate follow-up referencing 'up there in 3 hundreds' — the actual figure is very likely $300+/month, but this is Stewart's inference from context, not a clean verbatim capture.
coaching_implication: Note the transcription quality issue when reviewing this call with the rep — the manager should verify the actual bill number by listening to audio rather than relying on this transcript segment.

quote: Yeah. Well, I definitely see why you're kinda looking into, some savings options there on those bills.
stewart_read: The rep acknowledges the high bill but stops at generic validation ('I see why you're looking into savings') rather than flipping it into a pointed contrast against the utility or tying it forward to the appointment's purpose.
alternative_hypothesis: This could be read as an appropriate light-touch move for a setter call that shouldn't oversell — but the schema explicitly calls capture-then-move-on a failure_pattern distinct from ask+acknowledge+flip.
coaching_implication: Coach the rep to close the loop with something that ties the bill number forward — e.g., referencing that number again when framing why the appointment matters — rather than a generic acknowledgment that could apply to any customer.

quote: have you seen any solar information for your home before, or is this kind of your first time looking into it?
stewart_read: Customer discloses a prior solar look six-to-eight months ago, but the rep doesn't probe which company, what was shown, or why nothing happened — valuable competitive context for the closer is left uncollected.
alternative_hypothesis: The rep may have judged this detail unnecessary for a fast qualifying call, keeping to setter scope rather than digging into competitive history.
coaching_implication: A single follow-up ('who'd you look into last time, and what happened?') costs seconds and gives the closer real competitive intel — coach the rep to add this probe.

quote: Yeah. I could give you a call kinda tomorrow in the morning if that works good for you, and we can just get the rest of the information we need.
stewart_read: The call ends on a vague callback ('tomorrow in the morning') with no specific time locked and no 'is that fair?' handshake — this is procedural fragility, not a real customer barrier (the customer simply wasn't home).
coaching_implication: Coach the rep to lock a specific window ('does 9am or 10am work better?') and repeat it back before ending the call, even on a simple callback.

quote: Okay. Well, I'm not home right now.
stewart_read: The customer can't produce the bill on the call because he's away from home — a legitimate logistical block, not resistance. The rep correctly offers a callback rather than pushing.
alternative_hypothesis: This could be read as a soft decline/stall, but nothing in the tone suggests avoidance — the rep's own next line accepts it at face value and offers concrete alternatives.
coaching_implication: Handling is fine; the miss is only in not locking a specific callback time (see unanchored_soft_exit entry above).
